 :Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 25.06.2019 to 26.06.2019 at about 00.45 a.m. the Petitioner along with his friend one Puneet were proceeding in a Motorcycle bearing No.KA12Q2914 on Tumkur Bengaluru road and when they are proceeding opposite Parle G Factory and near to Navauga Toll, then one Lorry bearing No.KA53D 3339 was parked in the center of the road without switching on parking lights and no signals and as such,
the Petitioner while moving on the road because of the darkness failed to notice the parked lorry and dashed against the parked lorry.
As a result, the Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body and motorcycle was also damaged.

Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted Sri Sai Kanva Hospital at Bangalore and after taking first aid treatment he was shifted to Pinnacle Hospital,
Mysore road and he has undergone medical treatment and he was admitted as an inpatient in the said hospital.

sentences.text: The Petitioner has spent Rs.4,00,000/ towards medical expenses and other incidental expenses.
Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as Suggi Delivery boy and was earning Rs.25,000/ per month.
Due to the said accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.

The Respondent No.1 is the owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
3. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared before the Court through their respective Counsels.
But the Respondent No.1 did not choose to file Objection Statement.

The Respondent No.2 filed its Objection Statement to the main Petition interalia has denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle for parking the vehicle on the middle of the road without giving any signal.

On these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
4. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 26.06.2019 at about 00.45 a.m. NH4, TumkurBangalore, near Navayuga Toll,
Bengaluru, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Lorry bearing No.KA53 D3339?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
3 . What Order or Award ?

He also got examined two witnesses as P.W.2 and 3 and got marked 3 documents as per Ex.P.16 to P.19 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has examined its Administration Officer as RW.1 and got marked two documents as per Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 and closed its side evidence.

6. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondents and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order for the following :

He also got examined two other witnesses as P.W.2 and 3 and got marked 3 documents as per Ex.P.16 to P.19 .

14. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 has cross examined the P.W.1.
But nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the petitioner.

15. On the other hand, Respondent No.2 has examined its Administrative Officer by name Sri.

sentences.text: Moreover, after thorough investigation, the I.O. has filed Chargesheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is caused by the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
16. Issue No. 2 : As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the negligent parking of the offending vehicle without any signal by the driver of the offending vehicle, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
17. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 22 years.

Further, in the Aadhar card i.e.,
Ex.P10, the date of birth of the Petitioner was shown as 25.06.1998 and DL i.e., Ex.P11, the date of birth of the Petitioner was shown as 01.06.1998 .
The accident taken place on 25.06.2019.

Hence,
the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was 21 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
18.
Further, the petitioner has averred that he was working as Delivery boy at Suggi Daba and was earning Rs.25,000/ per month.
In this regard, he has not produced any documents to prove the income.

Therefore, in the absence of income proof, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, since the accident has been occurred in the year 2019, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e. 14,000/ p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
19. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
20.
The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P7 and other medical records reveals that in the accident the petitioner has sustained Fracture of both bones of left leg.
Further, the Doctor has opined that said injury is grievous in nature.
Further, P.W.2 has also re iterated about the grievous injuries sustained by the Petitioner.
21. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
22.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:

sentences.text: The petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient in Pinnacle hospital as an inpatient from 27.06.2019 to 05.07.2019.

has also reiterated the same in his evidence.
24. Upon going through Ex.P9 Discharge Summary which shows that the Petitioner was admitted in Pinnacle hospital as an inpatient from 27.06.2019 to 05.07.2019 i.e., for 9 days.
The total period which the petitioner was admitted as inpatient is 9 days.
25. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.28,000/ under this head (@ Rs.14,000/ per month ).
IV
COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :

26. Admittedly, the petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/ (@ Rs.100/ per month) towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/
towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/ under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
27. The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced 36 medical bills which totally marked at Ex.P.13.
I have gone through the said medical bills.
Upon going through the said medical bills, the total acceptable medical bills comes to Rs.1,98,569/.
Hence, by rounding of the same, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,98,600/ as a compensation under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :
28. The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is not able to do his work as he used to do earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.
Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as P.W.2 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.
Further, he got marked Clinical Notes and Xray at Ex.P.15 & Ex.P.16.
He assessed permanent physical disability of the left lower limb at 38% and whole body physical disability at 13%.
In the cross examination, he deposed that he is not personally treated the Petitioner.
Further he admitted that the fracture stated in his chiefexamination are simple fracture.

Further he admitted Sri Pavan C.Y vs Sri H. Gangarudraiah on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116390977/
6 that the fracture sustained by the Petitioner is completely cured.

sentences.text: He denied the other suggestions.

Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on record and evidence of P.W.2 and the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the petitioner with respect to the whole body at 8% would be just and proper.
As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 18.

With multiplier of 14, income of Rs.14,000/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 8%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.2,41,920/ (Rs.14,000/ x 12 =
1,68,000/, Rs.1,68,000/x 18 x 8/100 = Rs.2,41,920/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,41,920/ under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
29.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 40,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 40,000/
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 18,000/ diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 1,98,600/
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 28,000/ laid up period 6. Loss of Future income Rs.2,41,920 / Total Rs.5,66,520/
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.5,66,520/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.
30. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Lorry bearing No.No.KA53D3339.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy.
Therefore, both Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
31. Issue No. 3 :

In view of my findings on Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No. 1 and 2 U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
